properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: md-5@0.10.6 is a resolved dependency of the build via mongodb 2.8.2 (Cargo.lock:4984) — MongoDB's legacy SCRAM-SHA-1 authentication hashes the username with MD5. Not invoked by application code directly; it ships in the binary as the database auth stack. Changeable only by requiring SCRAM-SHA-256 on the MongoDB deployment, not in this repo.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: sha1@0.10.6 resolved via tungstenite 0.20.1/0.21.0 (RFC 6455 Sec-WebSocket-Accept — SHA-1 is hard-wired into the websocket handshake, a non-security use mandated by the protocol) and via headers 0.3.9 (web3's HTTP header types). No direct app call site; it ships with the WSS feed and web3 stacks.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Solana transaction-signature engine, exercised on every trade: read_keypair_file(PAYER_KEYPAIR_PATH) → Transaction::new_signed_with_payer (create_transaction.rs:188, :339, :387, :551) and send_and_confirm_transactions_in_parallel via Arc<dyn Signer> (:215, :414).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Scalar-arithmetic backend of ed25519-dalek 1.0.1 (Solana signature stack); no direct application use.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ring 0.16.20 supplies X25519 for rustls 0.21 on the QUIC TPU path (create_transaction.rs:199-207), and signs rcgen 0.10's ephemeral self-signed QUIC client certs.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: hmac 0.8.1 resolved via tiny-bip39 0.8.2 (solana-sdk 1.18's seed-phrase support): HMAC-SHA512 is the core of the BIP39 PBKDF2 that turns a mnemonic into the 512-bit seed. The primitive itself is quantum-safe; its posture here is as the BIP39 KDF engine. A second hmac 0.12.1 also ships (mongodb SCRAM, solana stack).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: pbkdf2 0.4.0 resolved via tiny-bip39 0.8.2 = the BIP39 standard KDF (PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512, 2048 iterations) deriving the seed from which Solana Keypairs can be reconstructed. 2048 iterations is far below modern OWASP guidance (CWE-916 territory) but the count is fixed by BIP39, not a local choice; the local control is not deriving production keys from phrases at all.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: sha2 0.9.9 resolved via tiny-bip39 0.8.2 — SHA-512/SHA-256 inside the BIP39 stack. Quantum-safe (Grover gives only a square-root speedup). Note the sibling sha2 0.10.8 (solana-program/solana-sdk, in shard 1's sha2 object) is the one behind live PDA-derivation hashing in this app.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: blake3 1.5.1 resolved via the solana stack (solana-runtime 1.18.15 at Cargo.lock:8711, solana-frozen-abi and related crates) — frozen-ABI / feature-set hashing. No application call site. Quantum-safe hash; keep.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ring 0.16.20's AES-GCM — TLS record protection for rustls 0.21.12 (quinn QUIC TPU sessions via ConnectionCache::new_quic at src/transactions/create_transaction.rs:202/401, and tungstenite 0.20 wss pubsub feeds). The AEAD itself is fine; the harvest-now-decrypt-later exposure sits in the ECDHE key exchange that seeds these session keys (see tls_key_exchange findings). A second ring 0.17.x also ships in the lockfile.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: System-OpenSSL bindings behind native-tls 0.2.12 (default TLS of reqwest 0.12.3); carries all HTTPS RPC and WSS pubsub traffic (RpcClient::new(env.rpc_url), ~10 sites in src/).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: native-tls 0.2.12 → platform OpenSSL (openssl 0.10.64 in the same lockfile). TLS backend for the bot's reqwest 0.12.3 (default-tls, used by make_request/src/common/utils.rs) and tungstenite 0.21 (tokio-tungstenite) — the HTTPS/WSS session family. Default ECDHE-only configuration, no post-quantum groups: harvest-now-decrypt-later exposure on all RPC/WS traffic.

properties.name: pqs:context

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Library-tier record of the same lockfile entry as ALG-70109388 (md-5@0.10.6, via mongodb 2.8.2 SCRAM-SHA-1). Kept so the dependency inventory and the algorithm view cross-reference one entry.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ring 0.16.20 in the shipped tree: provider for rustls 0.21 (QUIC X25519) and rcgen 0.10 (QUIC client-cert signing). 0.16.x is the abandoned line, pinned by solana 1.18's quinn.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ed25519-dalek 1.0.1 is THE Ed25519 engine behind solana-sdk's Keypair/Signer. Every Solana transaction this bot sends is signed through it: read_keypair_file loads the payer key, Transaction::new_signed_with_payer (create_transaction.rs:188/339/387/551), VersionedTransaction::try_new (:122), and re-sign loops in send_and_confirm_transactions_in_parallel (:219/:418). Shor-vulnerable signature; Ed25519 is the Solana protocol's signature scheme, so replacement is ecosystem-bound — observable here,

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: OpenSSL 0.10.64 bindings, pulled via native-tls 0.2.12 (reqwest/tungstenite TLS backend). Ships whatever the system OpenSSL provides at runtime — typically RSA, ECDHE, AES, SHA, TLS 1.2/1.3 and legacy algorithms depending on distro policy. No direct application call sites; the algorithm surface is observable here and replaceable only at the dependency level (move clients to rustls for PQ-hybrid readiness).

properties.name: pqs:context

properties.name: pqs:context

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: One of two hmac versions resolved (with 0.12.1 via ed25519-dalek-bip32/solana seed-phrase derivation); no direct application use.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: rustls 0.21.12 (ring-backed): TLS provider for quinn QUIC (solana TPU connection cache — ConnectionCache::new_quic at create_transaction.rs:202/401) and tungstenite 0.20 (wss pubsub feeds in src/markets/*). TLS 1.2/1.3 with ring ECDHE (X25519/P-256); the 0.21 line has no hybrid or PQ group support — that needs rustls ≥0.23 with ML-KEM hybrid key exchange. Harvest-now-decrypt-later exposure on the QUIC/WSS traffic.

properties.name: pqs:context
